title: Push a straw through the X-slot in a cold cup's lid, forcing its four flaps open, down to the bottom of the drink
instruction: Put the straw into the drink through the slot in the cup's lid, push it down to the bottom of the cup, and let go of it.
context: Anyone who has bought a cold drink to go knows this: the flat lid has an X-shaped straw slot, and the straw's end has to be aimed at the middle of the X and pushed until the four flaps between the cuts bend down and let it through, then pushed on down to the bottom so the last of the drink can be reached, and left standing in the slot. The straw is thin (6 mm) and light: aimed a few millimetres off the X it lands on the solid lid and goes nowhere, and pushed at a slant it can topple the tall, full cup (with 16 oz of drink, about 1.2 N sideways at the lid's top tips it over). Pushing it through takes about 5 N, more than a loosely held straw carries, so people grip it near the end that goes in, poke it through, then slide their fingers up and push it the rest of the way, as the robot must here.
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the counter (the table top). Nothing else is on the counter. 1) Cup: a Dart Solo Ultra Clear TP16D 16 oz clear PET cold cup, 98.4 across its rolled rim, 61.9 across its base, 120.7 tall, about 15 g, its inside bottom 3 above the counter; it holds 16 fl oz (473 ml) of cold cola, no ice (492 g; the surface about 17 below the rim). It stands with its base centred at (240, -60). 2) Lid, snapped on: a Dart Solo 626TS clear PET flat lid with straw slot, 101.2 across, 9.1 tall, about 3 g; its flat deck is 124.7 above the counter. The slot at the deck's centre is an X of two cuts, each 15.9 long, crossing at right angles; the four triangular flaps between them each bend down about the line joining the ends of their two cuts, 5.6 from the centre. Each flap's bend (estimates, no maker figure) yields at 0.0024 N m (0.0018 N m once moving) and springs back toward flat at 0.004 N m per radian: pushing the 6 mm straw's end through the centre takes about 5 N; bent fully open (62 degrees) the flaps press back on the straw and hold it. 3) Straw: a Choice 7 3/4 in jumbo black unwrapped plastic straw, 197 long, 6 across, about 0.45 g (simulated as 3 g), lying on the counter along x, its middle at (230, -190). Frictions (estimates): straw on the counter and lid 0.5, cup on the counter 0.4. Start: both arms at their ready pose, grippers open. The README lists every collider, hinge and mass.
scoring: Judged from the end of the run with a ruler and a photo through the clear cup. Through: the straw passes through the lid at the slot (its axis crosses the lid within 6 mm of the slot's centre) and its lower end is at least 10 mm below the lid's top. At depth: through, and its lower end within 20 mm of the cup's inside bottom (equivalently, its top stands no more than 95 mm above the lid). Let go: both grippers' centre points at least 3 cm from the straw and from the cup. Still: over the last 1 s each end of the straw and the cup moved less than 1 mm, and the straw's axis and the cup turned less than 2 degrees (a straw turning about its own axis counts as still). Scores: 1.0 at depth, let go and still, held for 1 s; 0.5 at depth but still held or moving, or through and let go and still but not at depth; 0.25 through but still held or moving; 0 for anything else: the straw not through the slot (on the counter, on the lid, in a hand), or the cup tipped more than 15 degrees at any moment, or more than 30 mm from its start mark at the end, or (real trials) its lid off the rim anywhere at the end or taken off at any time. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0.
reset_notes: Use a new lid each trial (the bent flaps do not spring fully flat again) and a new straw if it is kinked; top the cup back up to 473 ml, snap the lid on all round and stand the cup on its mark; lay the straw on its mark along x. Zero object jitter.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The lid is part of the cup (snapped on; nothing pulls it). Slot flaps: four hinged plates with a yield moment and a spring (estimates: about 5 N to push through), 0.2 g each with a numerical armature. Deck 0.8 mm, wall 1 mm thick (real about 0.25). The drink is a fixed mass: no liquid drag. The straw is rigid (a real one can kink) and weighs 3 g, not 0.45 g: lighter free parts are unstable in a pinch. Clear plastic renders opaque. Frictions are estimates.
